scope: A heuristic search record. Nothing here is an optimality proof: the kappa search (global class-level repack, ejection cycles, CP-SAT LNS including the evacuation neighbourhood) is finite and was stopped while still improving, and the min-diff step is a finite MIP/LNS. The surrogate ceiling below is not certified. Every shipped number is re-derived from data/ by verify.py (strict replay, seed67 audit, exact pricing, majorization check).
environment: CPython 3.12.14 via uv (uv run -q --no-project --python 3.12 --with ...), Linux x86_64, each job in a systemd scope with MemoryMax 4-6G, at most 2-3 workers. kappa search: numpy, ortools (CP-SAT). min-diff: numpy, scipy, highspy 1.15.1 (HiGHS, 1 thread), ortools (CP-SAT, 1 worker). ortools and highspy clash when loaded in one process, so mindiff_cls2.py runs its CP-SAT and HiGHS passes separately.

lineage.note: Search line: PR1407's map -> first version (two-stage cycles) -> second version's raw kappa search output (content a7e8f0ca...) -> global repack and cycle/LNS loop (third version; its min-diff map d05a885e...) -> evacuation LNS and loop (this version) -> min-diff toward the selected PR1094 map. Neither PR1407's map nor the earlier versions are exact ancestors of data/OWNERS.json.gz; the package is verified only against the selected map.

observations: On the third version's map many cap-48 bins held only a few small helpers (stranded bins). Emptying them needs their helpers to be re-packed into bins whose windows cover the same calls, which single cycles and call-set neighbourhoods rarely find.
kappa is close to linear in the surrogate sum f ln f over idle fragments; acceptance always uses the exact engines.
kappa_search.start: The third version's shipped map data/OWNERS.json.gz (content d05a885e8cc6a38dfbc9389e61769b4cb916ee858338e3fc3d6bcff6b877569d, kappa 0.001673054161426948, surrogate 906,246.66).
tools: search/lns.py mode evac (env NB, default 200): 1-3 stranded cap-48 bins (0 < used <= 20), bins with spare room (biased toward larger spare) and full bins whose allowed calls meet the stranded helpers' calls, plus 0, 2 or 5 empty bins allowing those calls; all their helpers are freed and re-packed exactly with CP-SAT (same surrogate objective and DIV plateau logic as the other modes). kappa values are now compared as Decimal.
search/loopy.sh (portable copy of the session's loopY.sh): loopx.sh with the mode mix evac, evac, time, time, f3, f3, evac, early15, time, f3.
kappa_search.how_it_ran: Interactively. One evac solve from the start map (102 bins in the neighbourhood; its seed and NB were not logged) emptied 35 cap-48 bins (+291 surrogate units, 906,246.66 -> 906,537.90) and gave kappa 0.001673213119136600. A loop started at the same time from the start map reached 0.001673163328271265 in about 15 minutes and was not continued. loopY.sh was then restarted from each strict-replayed best (bash $RANDOM seeds; at most two loops at a time, each job in a MemoryMax=4G scope); the segment from 0.001673243717212927 appears (from file times) to have used a variant, loopZ.sh, whose mode mix is weighted toward time and f3 (one evac in ten); the session did not log which script each segment ran. The best map has surrogate 906,773.72. The search was stopped while still improving (gains every 10-20 minutes near the end).

checkpoints.via: one lns.py evac solve (102 bins) from the third version map

kappa_search.stopped: Stopped at the end of the session's budget while still improving; no stall criterion was met.
kappa_search.tooling_bug: The session's loops compared kappa strings in lns.py (k > best_k); the pinned assembler can drop trailing zeros (0.0016732131191366 vs 0.001673213119136600), so a string comparison can misorder. Every checkpoint above was re-verified with Decimal comparisons, and the shipped lns.py, loopx.sh/loopy.sh, check.py and verify.py compare as Decimal.

surrogate_ceiling.status: Heuristic and not certified: the kappa-surrogate relation is approximate and the CP-SAT bound was not reproduced.

observations: kappa is close to linear in the surrogate sum f ln f over idle fragments (free capacities f > 1), so the surrogate is a usable global objective; acceptance always uses the exact engines.
Inside one physical family the bins' windows never overlap, so R4 reduces to at most one helper per bin per call.
Bins with the same capacity and the same set of allowed calls (144 classes of 224 bins) are interchangeable, so the packing becomes a class-level pattern/flow model.
Version 2's loop (chain2 ejection cycles plus CP-SAT LNS) had slowed to steps of about 1e-9 in kappa.
kappa_search.start: Version 2's raw kappa-search output F2 (content a7e8f0cac22527fd6f987b87c2734984add89166fd2d0306453bed99c25cee96, kappa 0.001672702955495933), not its min-diff map.
tools: search/glob.py: stage 1, CP-SAT over pattern counts x[class, pattern] and flows y[class, call, width] with per-(class, call) Hall constraints and optional Gale-Ryser-style constraints (GR=1), maximising the scaled surrogate; options S1ONLY, HINT, FIX, FREE, FIXTO, HALL.
search/glob5.py: stage 2, per-class and per-width max-flow realisation with distinct calls per bin over 40 random width orders; unplaced helpers inserted greedily where they cost the least surrogate.

search/loopx.sh (portable copy of the session's loopX.sh): chain2.py depth 8 while it improves, else one DIV=1 lns.py plateau step on a random mode (set:0,1,2,3,4, early8, early15, time, f3, fam); keeps the best map by exact kappa (score.py).
search/lns.py: as in version 2, plus NW (CP-SAT workers per solve) and the f3 mode.
kappa_search.how_it_ran: Interactively. glob.py was run several times with different time limits and options (best stage-1 objective 906,706 surrogate units; the start map had 905,605). The best stage 1 (906,706.49, CP-SAT bound 906,737.56 for that run's model, 1200 s) was realised by glob5.py; stage 2 left 80 helpers unplaced, which were inserted greedily. The realised map had kappa 0.001672432283943020, below the start, with a very different profile. loopx.sh from it (seeds from bash $RANDOM) reached 0.001672894024167899 in 43 steps; a second loopx.sh run from that map reached 0.001673054161426948. The exact flags of each glob.py run were not logged, so this phase is described, not replayable command by command.

tools: search/chain2.py (imports chain.py, lib.py): one- and two-stage ejection cycles, depth 8 in this phase

search/lns.py: CP-SAT large-neighbourhood re-assignment of all helpers of a set of calls (modes set:<calls>, time, early<k>, queue) or of physical families (fam); DIV=1 keeps the surrogate objective and randomly maximises relocations to move along plateaus
search/loop3.sh: alternates chain2.py until it finds nothing, then one DIV=1 lns.py step on a random mode
kappa_search.objective: Surrogate E = sum over (owner, child, port) bins of f ln f for free capacity f > 1 (CP-SAT scales it by 10^4 and rounds). Every candidate is audited with the seed67 rules and priced with the pinned exact engines; a step is kept only if the exact kappa rises (or, on a DIV plateau step, stays equal).
kappa_search.how_it_ran: Interactively, in order: lns.py time/set neighbourhoods from the first version's map; lns.py set:0,1,2,3,4 with 400-900 s CP-SAT limits; chain2.py depth 8; then loop.sh, loop2.sh and loop3.sh runs (loop2.sh is loop3.sh with a different mode list; loop3.sh is shipped). Seeds partly come from bash $RANDOM, so the trajectory is not reproducible bit for bit.

checkpoints.via: loop2.sh then loop3.sh (chain2 + DIV lns alternation)

first_version.environment: CPython 3.12.14 + numpy (uv run -q --no-project --python 3.12 --with numpy), Linux x86_64, MemoryMax=5G scope, one worker
first_version.objective: Relaxed surrogate E = sum over (owner, child, port) bins of f ln f for free capacity f > 1; candidate cycles found by a max-plus DP over (hand width, hand time) states, then replayed exactly with the seed67 auditor geometry and priced with the pinned exact engines. E is only a search heuristic; kappa comes from the exact engines.
